profiles.name: Lobito Corridor
profiles.summary: Freight from the Democratic Republic of the Congo already reaches the Atlantic by rail through Angola. Zambia’s proposed line would join that railway at Luacano and give Chingola a route to Lobito.
profiles.qualification: The African Development Bank’s May 2026 appraisal puts the proposed extension at 829 kilometres.
profiles.statusScope: Corridor designation and the individual components identified below

paragraphs.text: The proposed railway runs from Chingola to Luacano. West of the junction, Zambian freight would travel on the existing line to the port of Lobito.
The African Development Bank assigns about 550 kilometres of new track to Zambia and 279 to Angola. These figures exclude the existing line west of Luacano.

events.text: The bank’s appraisal sets out the route and scope of the proposed Zambia connection.

focus.alt: The port of Lobito in Angola, photographed in 2015.

profiles.name: Rhine-Danube Corridor
profiles.summary: The Rhine-Danube corridor has two distinct geographies. Strasbourg anchors its southern routes. In 2024, the northern branch extended the designation from German seaports to Lviv.
profiles.qualification: The map traces a stretch of the Danube within a wider network of roads, railways and waterways.
profiles.statusScope: Corridor designation and the individual components identified below

paragraphs.text: East of Strasbourg, one branch follows the Main, the Main-Danube Canal and the Danube. The other passes through Stuttgart and Munich. They meet in Austria.
The 2024 revision brought connections through Dresden and Prague into the northern branch and extended the corridor to Lviv in Ukraine.

events.text: The northern segment became part of the Rhine-Danube Corridor.

profiles.name: Trans-Kalahari Corridor
profiles.summary: Road freight travels from Walvis Bay across Botswana to Gauteng in South Africa. Rail serves parts of the same corridor, with separate connections at Gobabis in Namibia and Lobatse in Botswana.
profiles.qualification: The Walvis Bay Corridor Group identifies rail connections at Gobabis and Lobatse. Its description establishes no rail link between the two.
profiles.statusScope: Corridor designation and the individual components identified below

paragraphs.text: The Namibian railway runs from Walvis Bay through Windhoek to Gobabis, where cargo can transfer between modes. In Botswana, the corridor meets the railway at Lobatse.
UNCTAD’s 2007 inventory distinguishes the route across Botswana to South Africa from the Trans-Cunene route north to Lubango. Both use Walvis Bay.

events.text: The three participating governments officially opened the corridor.
UNCTAD documented the Walvis Bay connection to Gaborone and Johannesburg.

profiles.name: Trans-Cunene Corridor
profiles.summary: Walvis Bay gives southern Angola a route to the Atlantic through Namibia. On the journey north to Lubango, the road crosses the border and the Namibian railway ends at Oshikango.
profiles.qualification: The Walvis Bay Corridor Group identifies the cross-border rail link as a proposal.
profiles.statusScope: Corridor designation and the individual components identified below

paragraphs.text: The road crosses into Angola at Santa Clara and continues to Lubango. The proposed railway would link the Angolan and Namibian rail systems.

sections.title: The second route from Walvis Bay

paragraphs.text: In its 2007 inventory, UNCTAD lists Walvis Bay as the gateway for Trans-Cunene and Trans-Kalahari. The former serves southern Angola. The latter crosses Botswana to South Africa.

events.text: Angola and Namibia agreed to establish the corridor.
UNCTAD documented the Walvis Bay connection to Lubango.

profiles.name: Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project
profiles.summary: Cargo bound for Mizoram changes mode twice under the Kaladan plan. At Sittwe it leaves the sea for the river. At Paletwa the onward route depends on a road to the Indian border.
profiles.qualification: India’s August 2026 update dates completion of the waterway to May 2023. It gives no completion date for the highway.
profiles.statusScope: Corridor designation and the individual components identified below

paragraphs.text: A cargo vessel from Kolkata arrived for the opening of Sittwe port in May 2023. Sittwe is the transfer point for river traffic to Paletwa, where the planned road leg begins.
India’s August 2026 update puts the highway from Paletwa to Zorinpui at 109 kilometres. The ministry identifies the waterway as the completed component.

events.text: Officials in Myanmar received the inaugural cargo vessel from Kolkata at Sittwe.
The regional development ministry reported completion of the waterway component and described the separate road component.

profiles.name: Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec
aliases: Corredor Interoceánico del Istmo de Tehuantepec
profiles.summary: Line Z links the Pacific port of Salina Cruz to Coatzacoalcos on the Gulf of Mexico. The railway forms part of a wider corridor authority whose remit includes four port administrations and development sites.
profiles.qualification: On 5 June 2026, Mexico’s presidency reported continuing freight operations and a suspension of passenger service.
profiles.statusScope: Corridor designation and the individual components identified below

paragraphs.text: The corridor statute divides Line Z at Medias Aguas. It places four port administrations within the authority’s remit, covering Coatzacoalcos, Salina Cruz, Dos Bocas and Puerto Chiapas.
In June 2026, Mexico’s president said freight continued to run while passenger service was suspended for safety reasons. The statement distinguishes the two services at the time of the briefing.

events.text: Mexico’s presidency reported that freight was operating while passenger service was suspended.

profiles.name: Northern Corridor (East Africa)
aliases: Northern Corridor Transit and Transport Agreement
profiles.summary: The port of Mombasa serves inland markets across the Great Lakes region. The Northern Corridor agreement governs transit across national borders, while carriers can choose between road crossings into Uganda and Rwanda.
profiles.qualification: The map traces a section of the Mombasa road between Mazeras and Mariakani and marks eight towns named by the corridor authority. The road centreline shows its general alignment. It does not establish lane configuration or through freight service.
profiles.statusScope: Treaty framework and identified road routes

paragraphs.text: The authority describes a main road via Malaba and a second approach via Kisumu and Busia. Beyond Kampala, it identifies separate crossings at Kagitumba and Gatuna on the way to Kigali.
The original agreement entered into force in 1986. Its 2007 revision broadened the mandate to include investment and development. South Sudan became the sixth member in 2012.

events.text: The original transit agreement entered into force.
The revised agreement was signed in Nairobi.
South Sudan joined the agreement.

profiles.name: Greater Mekong East-West Economic Corridor
aliases: Greater Mekong Subregion East-West Economic Corridor
profiles.summary: The route named in the regional transport agreement runs from Mawlamyine in Myanmar to Da Nang in Viet Nam through Thailand and the Lao PDR. The Greater Mekong ministers later endorsed a western extension to Yangon and Thilawa.
profiles.qualification: The map identifies selected towns and part of National Highway 9 between Cam Lo and Dong Ha. The traced section establishes local road geography. Border procedures and through services require separate evidence.
profiles.statusScope: Regional designation, with individual road projects assessed separately

paragraphs.text: The transport agreement pairs Myawaddy with Mae Sot at the Myanmar-Thailand border, Mukdahan with Savannakhet across the Mekong, and Dansavanh with Lao Bao on the approach to Viet Nam. These pairs identify where the designated route passes from one jurisdiction to the next.

On the Vietnamese section, an ADB project covered about 83 kilometres of Road 9 from Lao Bao to Dong Ha, including work on the Dong Ha bypass. A 2008 evaluation found better road transport efficiency between Dong Ha and Kaysone Phomvihane in the Lao PDR. It found less progress in reducing administrative obstacles to cross-border movement.

In its August 2017 account the GMS Secretariat recorded ministerial endorsement of a western branch through Bago to Yangon and Thilawa. It described a further extension to Pathein as a possibility. This distinction matters when reading maps from different editions of the corridor programme.

events.text: ADB approved the Vietnamese Road 9 improvement project between the Lao border and Dong Ha.
ADB published its evaluation of the road and border facilitation project in the Lao PDR and Viet Nam.
The GMS Secretariat reported that ministers had endorsed the Yangon-Thilawa extension.

profiles.name: Beira Corridor
profiles.summary: From the port of Beira, the railway crosses central Mozambique to Machipanda on the Zimbabwean border.
profiles.qualification: The African Union’s infrastructure programme gives 317 kilometres for the Beira-Machipanda project. The map shows an inland section of that line through Chimoio.
profiles.statusScope: Mozambican port and railway to Machipanda

paragraphs.text: Mozambique inaugurated the rehabilitated railway on 23 November 2023. At the ceremony in Manica, the president announced that passenger trains between Beira and Machipanda would resume the following week.
The state railway recorded 165,460 net tonnes on the Machipanda line in 2024, down from 207,790 in 2023. Its table counts freight on this railway. The port also handles cargo from other routes.

events.text: Mozambique inaugurated the rehabilitated Machipanda railway in Manica.

profiles.name: Nacala Corridor
profiles.summary: The Northern Railway links the port of Nacala to Malawi through northern Mozambique. Moatize coal uses a separate maritime outlet at Nacala-à-Velha.
profiles.qualification: The map locates the port in Nacala City and a section of the Northern Railway through Nampula. In 2023 Mozambique, Malawi and Zambia signed a partnership on the wider corridor.
profiles.statusScope: Mozambican port and rail assets and their documented links to Malawi

paragraphs.text: Mozambique inaugurated the upgraded port in Nacala City on 7 October 2023. For 2024 the national port statistics list 3.55 million tonnes at Nacala and 13.87 million tonnes at Nacala-à-Velha, the dedicated coal outlet.
In August 2023 a train carried 1.1 million litres of diesel in 29 tank wagons. The port handbook records this consignment as the first in a renewed fuel trade with Malawi.

events.text: Mozambique inaugurated the upgraded port in Nacala City. At the ceremony, Mozambique, Malawi and Zambia signed a corridor development partnership.

profiles.name: Middle Corridor
profiles.summary: Trains from China enter Kazakhstan at Dostyk or Altynkol. Freight travels west to the Caspian, crosses by ship to Azerbaijan, and continues by rail through Georgia. From there it can take a Black Sea sailing or the rail route through Türkiye.
profiles.qualification: Samruk-Kazyna reported 0.8 million tonnes of transit freight on the route in 2025. That figure describes transit cargo. The same report gives container traffic in twenty-foot equivalent units, a different measure.
profiles.statusScope: Rail and sea freight services and the individual investments described here

sections.title: The Caspian crossing and the Georgian branches

paragraphs.text: Kazakhstan has two gateways on the Caspian crossing. Ships carry containers between Aktau and Alat in Azerbaijan. Ferries at Kuryk serve trucks and rail wagons. The commercial Port of Baku moved to Alat in 2018, about 70 kilometres southwest of Baku.
In Georgia, freight can reach the Black Sea ports of Poti and Batumi by rail. Another branch runs from Tbilisi through Akhalkalaki towards Kars in Türkiye.

The route association’s 2025 schedule listed US$1,869 for a loaded 20-foot container from Altynkol to Batumi or Poti via Aktau and Alat. The reverse journey was listed at US$1,033. The rates applied from January to December 2025 under the schedule’s loading and consignment conditions.

For an onward Black Sea crossing to Constanța, the tariff notes required confirmation when booking. A consignor could therefore use the dated table to compare directions to the Georgian ports. A current delivered price for a European customer requires an onward quotation.

In its 2025 annual report, Samruk-Kazyna recorded 41,500 twenty-foot equivalent units of container traffic and 0.8 million tonnes of transit freight. The two figures cannot be added. It also described the joint venture established by the Kazakh, Azerbaijani and Georgian railways to coordinate multimodal services.

On 19 February 2026 the World Bank approved a US$846 million guarantee intended to mobilise US$1.41 billion in long-term commercial finance for Kazakhstan’s railway project. The guarantee supports financing for one country’s section. Adding its value to the target financing would count the guarantee as a second investment.

events.text: The route association’s 2025 feeder-vessel tariff period began for specified container movements via Alat.
The published 2025 feeder-vessel tariff period ended.
The World Bank approved a guarantee for the Kazakhstan rail connectivity project.

profiles.name: India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor
profiles.summary: IMEC proposes to connect India with the Arabian Gulf by sea and continue to Europe through a combination of rail and sea transport. Its defining commercial question is whether separate ports, rail networks and customs authorities can offer a continuous freight journey.
profiles.qualification: India’s maritime administration reported in October 2026 that rail gaps, port connections, financing and transit procedures remained unresolved. Its map illustrates possible gateways. The precise terminals and rail alignment still require agreement among the implementing partners.
profiles.statusScope: The proposed international freight corridor as a whole

sections.title: Who signed, and where freight would travel

paragraphs.text: At New Delhi on 9 September 2023, India, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, France, Germany, Italy and the United States signed the memorandum alongside the European Union. The EU participated in its own right. Jordan and Israel appear in the proposed transit geography and are absent from the list of signatories.

sections.title: Two freight legs and three utility proposals

paragraphs.text: The memorandum divides the project at the Arabian Gulf. Its eastern leg would connect the Gulf with India. The northern leg would combine cross-border rail with a further sea crossing to Europe. The participants also envisaged power cables, digital links and a pipeline for clean hydrogen along the railway.

sections.title: From a political commitment to customs cooperation

paragraphs.text: The memorandum records a political commitment and expressly disclaims rights or obligations under international law. India and the UAE took a separate bilateral step in February 2024. Their framework covers port, shipping and logistics cooperation and the exploration of joint investment.

The two governments subsequently launched work on a virtual trade corridor. India’s MAITRI interface is intended to connect customs and logistics platforms across the two countries. In March 2025 the Indian embassy reported that developers were working with Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority, Deendayal Port and other Indian ports.

India’s October 2026 maritime report illustrates an Indian gateway in the Mumbai and Jawaharlal Nehru Port area and a Mediterranean transfer at Haifa. The atlas marks Mumbai at city scale and Haifa at port scale. The report leaves the terminal choices open and identifies missing connections between existing transport systems.

events.text: Seven states and the European Union signed the IMEC memorandum in New Delhi.
India and the UAE signed a bilateral framework for cooperation on the corridor.
India’s embassy in Abu Dhabi reported joint work on linking trade portals and identified participating Indian port authorities.

profiles.name: Interstate 69 Corridor
profiles.statusScope: Federal designation and individual state highway projects
profiles.summary: Interstate 69 links operating highways with projects under development between Michigan and Texas. At Evansville, Indiana has finished the approach for a new Ohio River bridge. Through traffic depends on the crossing itself.
profiles.qualification: The mapped lines follow Indiana road records carrying the I-69 name in the 2025 federal inventory. Shared pavement can carry another interstate name. The map omits proposed alignments and gives no national completion figure.

paragraphs.text: In August 2024 the new interchange south of Indianapolis joined I-69 to the I-465 beltway. I-69 shares pavement with I-465 around part of the city and with I-74 for a shorter stretch. A route number can therefore continue across a section named for another highway in a road inventory.

sections.title: Two contracts at the Ohio River

paragraphs.text: Indiana completed its $202 million approach project in September 2026. Three approach bridges and connecting roads give crews access to the river in wet weather. Their opening to motorists depends on completion of the new bridge between Evansville and Henderson.

Kentucky finished a highway extension in Henderson in late 2025. A separate contract covers the four-lane river bridge and its connections on both banks. The two states can complete approach works at different times while the crossing remains a joint undertaking.

Texas is upgrading existing roads, including US 59 toward Laredo and US 77 toward Brownsville. Once a segment meets interstate standards, the state seeks approval for its designation. TxDOT identifies no dedicated appropriation for construction of its entire I-69 system.

The atlas draws the Indiana features named I-69 in the Census Bureau’s 2025 primary and secondary roads file. The geographic extent is one state. Federal corridor designation and the operating status of an individual segment answer different questions.

events.text: The I-69/I-465 interchange on the south side of Indianapolis opened to traffic.
The Census Bureau released the 2025 TIGER/Line edition used for the Indiana alignment.
Indiana announced completion of its Ohio River approach contract. The roads serve bridge construction until the new crossing opens.

profiles.name: Rhine-Alpine Corridor, historical
profiles.summary: The European Union used the Rhine-Alpine designation for a network connecting the North Sea ports of Rotterdam and Antwerp to Genoa through the Rhine valley and Switzerland. The statutory alignment included branches through both Milan and Novara.
profiles.qualification: From 18 July 2024 the North Sea-Rhine-Mediterranean Corridor brought the former Rhine-Alpine and North Sea-Mediterranean core corridors together. The dates below delimit the former planning designation. The cities, ports and railways have their own histories.
profiles.statusScope: Former multimodal TEN-T core network corridor designation

sections.title: From the delta to the Alpine crossings

paragraphs.text: The 2013 regulation set out branches to the Dutch and Belgian ports through Duisburg or Liège. South of Basel it traced a western route by Bern, Brig and Novara and an eastern route by Lugano and Milan. Both reached Genoa. The map markers identify selected cities in this historical alignment.

The 2020 coordinator’s work plan mapped railways, roads and inland waterways separately. Swiss representatives participated in the corridor forum, and the coordinator included Swiss projects in the analysis. On the railway north of Switzerland, Karlsruhe to Basel was among the sections where the coordinator anticipated capacity constraints beyond 2030. That was a forecast made in 2020.

Under the 2024 regulation the European Commission describes the former Rhine-Alpine and North Sea-Mediterranean corridors as components of a single successor. The expanded designation also covers a western axis from Le Havre through Paris and Lyon. Adding the lengths for the old and new designations would count inherited sections twice.

sections.title: An Alpine railway after the designation changed

paragraphs.text: Swiss Federal Railways reported that the Gotthard Base Tunnel returned to unrestricted passenger and freight service on 2 September 2024 after the derailment of August 2023. The tunnel’s reopening concerned train operations and took place after the European planning designation had changed.

events.text: The Connecting Europe Facility regulation began to apply, with the Rhine-Alpine alignment listed in its first annex.
The revised TEN-T regulation took effect. Its maps included the North Sea-Rhine-Mediterranean successor corridor.

profiles.name: Paraguay-Paraná Waterway
profiles.summary: Five countries share a river transport agreement linking Cáceres in Brazil with Nueva Palmira in Uruguay. It covers the Paraguay and Paraná rivers, the Paraná’s outlet channels and the Tamengo Canal on the Brazil-Bolivia border.
profiles.qualification: The map follows the rivers from Asunción in Paraguay to Rosario in Argentina. Its line shows the general river course at atlas scale. Channel depths and the positions of navigation buoys require current river charts.
profiles.statusScope: International river transport agreement and a mapped reach between Paraguay and Argentina

paragraphs.text: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay signed the agreement on 26 June 1992. It entered into force on 13 February 1995. Article 9 permits vessels, goods and people from member countries to transit the waterway and allows charges for services actually provided.

On 2 November 2024, the gauge at the port of Asunción read 1.61 metres below its zero mark. Paraguay’s hydrological service identified this as the lowest reading in the station record, which began in 1904. The measurement describes the river level at that gauge.

events.text: The five governments signed the waterway agreement.
The gauge at Asunción recorded the lowest river level in its series dating from 1904.

profiles.name: Highlands Highway, Papua New Guinea
profiles.statusScope: Existing highway and ongoing investment in its road and bridge assets
profiles.summary: The Highlands Highway links Lae’s port with the coffee-growing districts of Papua New Guinea’s interior. West of Goroka the road crosses Daulo Pass, descends to Kundiawa and continues to Mount Hagen.
profiles.qualification: The map traces a central portion of the road through Goroka and Kundiawa. Its western endpoint lies east of Mount Hagen. The markers for the port and highland towns identify places along the wider route.

sections.title: From the port into the mountains

paragraphs.text: From Lae the highway follows the Markham Valley before climbing past Kassam Pass. Trucks serving the coffee districts of Kainantu and Goroka share the trunk road with freight moving farther west. Beyond Mount Hagen, branches serve Mendi and the mining route through Wabag toward Porgera.

Farmers use the highway to reach buyers and the coast. For growers shipping fresh produce, a delay at a damaged bridge or a landslide can cost the value of a shipment if the crop spoils before it reaches a buyer. The road’s value to producers depends on how reliably it can be used between repairs.

ADB’s highway investment programme covers about 430 kilometres between the Nadzab and Kagamuga airport junctions. The second tranche targets 71 bridges. On 14 September 2026 the prime minister announced the commissioning of the BCW3-16 bridge package at Mount Hagen.

ADB’s independent evaluation counted works across 428 kilometres under the first tranche, including 43 kilometres of reconstruction. The agreed US$10 million road maintenance allocation did not materialise. Some improved stretches deteriorated within two years, leaving the reliability of the route dependent on funding after construction.

events.text: ADB approved the first tranche loans for the highway investment programme.
The prime minister announced commissioning of the BCW3-16 bridge package at Mount Hagen.
ADB’s independent evaluation reported rapid deterioration on some rehabilitated sections and a shortfall in maintenance funding.

profiles.name: Inland Rail
profiles.summary: Australia’s Inland Rail programme envisages double-stacked container trains between Melbourne and Brisbane. The federal government prioritised delivery between Beveridge in Victoria and Parkes in New South Wales. Farther north, the completed railway to Narromine and the sections reserved for possible future works have different statuses.
profiles.qualification: The mapped line follows existing railway between Stockinbingal and Parkes, where Inland Rail reported the completion of upgrades in January 2026. The 170.3 kilometres describe the existing section on which specific sites were modified.
profiles.statusScope: Australian Inland Rail programme, with separate milestones for named sections

sections.title: The railway shown on the map

paragraphs.text: The line follows Geoscience Australia’s 2021 mapping of the existing Stockinbingal to Parkes railway. It records the track corridor before the later clearance works. Melbourne and Brisbane locate the programme’s intended endpoints. The atlas plots the cities at representative locations, and traces only the documented New South Wales section.

sections.title: How the upgrade changed the railway

paragraphs.text: At Forbes, contractors lowered the track under the Wyndham Avenue road bridge to provide headroom for containers carried two high. At Daroobalgie, a new 2.2-kilometre crossing loop gave trains a place to pass. In January 2026 Stockinbingal to Parkes became the third programme section reported fully operational.

The Australian Rail Track Corporation received the completed Parkes to Narromine section in 2020. In May 2026 the federal government confirmed its priority was delivery to Parkes and preservation farther north. The promoter identifies the sections north of Narromine for future consideration. Protecting the alignment keeps open a future construction decision.

On 23 November 2026 Inland Rail reported that all 12 enhancement sites between Beveridge and Albury provided clearance for double-stacked freight, including the Tallarook passing loop. Station works were continuing at Euroa and Benalla. The announcement establishes local clearance. It gives no date for a continuous double-stacked service to Brisbane.

events.text: Inland Rail records completion of the upgrade to the Stockinbingal to Parkes section in January. Its February release identifies it as the third section ready for double-stacked operations.
The Australian government confirmed delivery to Parkes as the programme priority and preservation of the corridor farther north.
Inland Rail reported that its 12 Victorian enhancement sites had the clearance required for double-stacked freight.

profiles.name: China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor
profiles.summary: The three governments adopted an economic cooperation programme in 2016. Its central railway connects the Russian city of Ulan-Ude with Ulaanbaatar and the Chinese cities of Beijing and Tianjin. Freight crosses between Mongolia and China at Zamyn-Uud and Erenhot.
profiles.qualification: The map shows a short railway section at the Mongolia-China border and individual towns named on the rail or highway itineraries. The documents establish the programme and its geography. They do not establish a current through timetable, freight rate or journey time.
profiles.statusScope: Trilateral programme and separately documented rail and road components

paragraphs.text: The 2016 outline identified 32 priority projects. Alongside infrastructure, China’s foreign ministry listed industrial cooperation, customs, border facilities and environmental protection. In September 2025 the three leaders agreed to extend the programme through 2031.

sections.title: What changes at the rail border

paragraphs.text: The central railway itinerary places Zamyn-Uud and Erenhot on opposite sides of the same frontier. A CAREC monitoring report recorded delays associated with the change of rail gauge at these crossings. Those observations describe the 2011 monitoring period. They cannot establish present waiting times.

sections.title: The highway has its own agreement

paragraphs.text: China, Mongolia and Russia signed a separate road transport agreement in December 2016. ESCAP records its entry into force in September 2018. Its AH3 map names Kyakhta, Darkhan and Ulaanbaatar on the way from Ulan-Ude to Tianjin. These are road itinerary points, separate from the mapped railway section.

events.text: Government departments of the three countries signed the economic corridor outline at Tashkent.
The separate trilateral road transport agreement entered into force.
The three leaders agreed in Beijing to extend the corridor programme through 2031.
